summary: This RFC is the official specification of the Hostname Server Protocol, a service for fetching host table information from a server. It revises RFC 811 and is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: The Hostname Server lets a program ask for host information such as a name or address. Each TCP connection carries one request, and the server closes it after replying.

subtitle: A TCP service for looking up entries in the Internet host table.

tldr.problem: Programs needed a machine-readable service for finding names and addresses of Internet networks, gateways and hosts.
tldr.mechanism: A client opens a TCP connection, sends one text command, reads the response and then the server closes the connection.
tldr.outcome: RFC 953 is Historic and obsoletes RFC 811; the protocol supports host lookups and full-table requests.

today: RFC 953 is Historic and obsoletes RFC 811. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes RFC 953.

sections.title: Host and Network Information
sections.content: The NIC Internet Hostname Server is a TCP-based program and protocol running on SRI-NIC. It provides machine-readable name and address information about networks, gateways, hosts and, eventually, domains. As implemented, it supplies information described by the DoD Internet Host Table specification.
sections.plainLanguage: A program can use the server to look up Internet host information in a format it can read. The server can return names and addresses for hosts and other network entries.

sections.title: One Request per TCP Connection
sections.content:
A client connects to TCP port 101 on the service host, sends one request line and reads the response. The server closes the connection when the response is complete, so a client makes only one request on each connection. Requests use a command key, arguments and optional options; responses begin with a response key.

HNAME searches by host name, HADDR searches by host address, and ALL returns the full host table. The server also defines commands such as HELP, VERSION and DOMAINS.
sections.plainLanguage: The client opens a connection, asks one question and reads the answer. To ask another question, it opens another connection.

sections.title: Responses and Errors
sections.content:
Responses start with a key such as HOST, NET, GATEWAY, DOMAIN or ERR. A large response may span multiple lines, with continuation lines beginning with a space. An ALL response begins with BEGIN and ends with END.

An error response includes a short code and a message. Defined codes include NAMNFD for a missing name, ADRNFD for a missing address, ILLCOM for an unrecognized command and TMPSYS for a temporary system failure.
sections.plainLanguage: The first word of a reply tells the client what kind of information follows. If something goes wrong, the reply gives an error code and a short explanation.
